impact:
`src/config.ts` does `p.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, "-")` with no `u` flag, so it iterates UTF-16 code units. `usage.py`'s `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", p)` iterates code points. Any non-BMP character (emoji, CJK Ext-B, math alphanumerics) in a path yields TWO dashes in the port and ONE in Python.

Measured:
  PY   : re.sub -> "-Users-testuser"
  JS   : .replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g,"-")  -> "-Users-testuser"
  JS+u : .replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/gu,"-") -> "-Users-testuser"   (matches Python)

Two reachable consequences:
1. Codex path — the port does the encoding itself (`codex.ts` -> `cleanName(encodePath(cwd))`, where `cwd` comes out of the rollout log's `session_meta`), so a project whose path contains an emoji is labelled differently than Python labels it.
2. `deps.homeEnc` — with an astral character in $HOME the encoded prefix differs, so prefix stripping fails and the displayed project name changes shape entirely (measured: Python "~/-Developer-alpha" vs port "alpha").

Both sides exit 0 and print different output, so no test or golden catches it. Not covered by any ALLOWLIST entry.

PRE-EXISTING and out of T-006's scope: `src/config.ts` is untouched by this ticket, and the defect is independent of anything T-006 changed. Filed rather than fixed inline per the autonomous-session rule. (The sibling finding in `aggregate.ts` WAS fixed in T-006, because T-006's own requireString relaxation is what made it reachable — different situation.)

FIX: add the `u` flag. Add a differential test against CPython's `re.sub` over a set of astral code points, in the style of the existing digitValue/isprintable CPython differentials.

Found by code review R6 (agent, parity lens) via an end-to-end Python-vs-port comparison on a rollout fixture with an emoji cwd.
title: encodePath splits astral characters into two dashes; Python produces one
